title: Isolation, cultivation, and application of primary respiratory epithelial cells obtained by nasal brushing, polyp samples, or lung explants
protocol: Prepare 2 × 15 mL tubes with 2.5 mL of room temperature PBS (or FertiCult).
Label the tubes with the subject’s identification/reference number and the date of sampling, put aside.
Fill in the information sheet provided with the subject’s identification number/tag, the genotype, and antibiotic resistance profiles of bacterial strains isolated from the subject if possible.
Sterilize the nose speculum with 70% ethanol or other approved sterilizing solution that is not harmful to humans.
Sterilize Politzer tweezers.
Assemble four flat cotton meshes: two approximately 5 cm and two approximately 10 cm long.
Roll one end of each mesh into a cone shape.
Ask the subject to clean or blow their nose.
Instruct the subject to sit comfortably in a chair.
Inform the subject that eye watering may occur but will quickly resolve.
Tilt the subject’s head backwards.
Examine the nostrils with a speculum to identify the inferior turbinate.
Soak four strands of cotton in xylocaine 5% with naphazoline solution.
Squeeze off any excess liquid from the soaked cotton meshes.
Roll one end of each mesh to be introduced into the nostril first.
Tilt the subject’s head backwards.
Introduce one cotton mesh per nostril using Politzer tweezers for horizontal movement.
Leave the cotton meshes in situ for 5 minutes.
Remove the initial set of cotton meshes after 5 minutes.
Prepare a second set of longer cotton meshes (approximately 10 cm).
Introduce the longer cotton meshes into the nostrils using Politzer tweezers.
Leave these longer meshes in situ for an additional 5 minutes.
Introduce one cotton mesh per nostril using Politzer tweezers.
Push the cotton mesh as far as possible after initial insertion.
Leave the cotton meshes in place for at least 10 minutes.
Remove the cotton meshes from each nostril.
Ask the subject to blow their nose once more.
Wet the nasal brush with sterile PBS or sterile FertiCult in a 15 mL conical tube.
Introduce the nasal brush horizontally along the passage between the inferior and middle turbinate.
Brush at the lower turbinate in the middle third with five to ten rotational and linear movements.
Remove the brush from the nostril.
Place the brush in a tube with sterile PBS.
Shake the brush vigorously in the medium for 15 seconds.
If an endoscopy brush is used, sweep/scrape the brush using the plastic sheath.
Obtain at least one brushing per nostril.
Ideally, brush each nostril twice if possible.
Use the same brush for subsequent brushings of the same nostril.
Shake the brush in the labeled tube after the last brushing.
Cut the remaining wire to allow the brush to fit entirely into the tube.
Seal the labeled tube and set aside on ice or in the fridge.
Repeat the procedure with the other nostril.
If FertiCult was used, add 0.1 mL of antibiotic solution to each labeled tube containing the samples using a sterile procedure.
Remove as many cells as possible from the brush using the sheath from the wire.
Discard the brush after removing the cells.
Centrifuge the tube contents at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Gently aspirate and discard the supernatant without touching the pellet.
Add 0.5 mL of Trypsin to the pellets, resuspend the cells, and incubate at 37°C for 5–7 minutes.
Add 1 mL of amplification medium to stop the enzymatic process.
Combine the contents of both tubes and mix gently.
Centrifuge the combined sample at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of amplification medium.
Evenly distribute the cell suspension into collagen-coated flasks.
Add 10 mL of amplification medium to each 75 cm² flask.
Add 5 mL of amplification medium to each 25 cm² flask.
Place the flasks in the incubator at 37°C.
Check cells 24 hours after culture initiation.
Allow a minimum of 12 hours for cell adhesion.
Brush a single nostril and seed it in one 25 cm² flask.
Transport lung explant samples in PBS or culture medium on wet ice.
Add the lung explants, including transport media, into a 10 cm Petri dish.
Conduct all procedures under sterile conditions.
Use a scalpel blade or disposable stainless-steel lancets to remove and discard necrotic parts of the bronchi.
Place the cleaned piece of the bronchi into an empty 50 mL tube.
Wash the bronchi twice with PBS-DTT-FTVC at room temperature (18°C–23°C) by adding 25 mL of the solution, shaking manually for 30 seconds, and aspirating the media.
Repeat steps i. and ii. to ensure thorough washing.
Rinse the bronchi with PBS-FTVC by adding 25 mL of the solution, shaking for 30 seconds, and aspirating the media.
Repeat steps i. and ii. to complete the rinsing process.
Fill the tube containing the explant with 14 mL of pre-prepared DMEM/F12-FTVC medium.
Add 4 mL of Pronase to the 50 mL tube containing now only 36 mL of DMEM/F12-FTVC.
Aspirate the 14 mL of medium from step d.
Transfer the bronchi into the DMEM/F12-FTVC-Pronase solution.
Incubate the bronchi overnight at 4°C on a rotator (12 h for best results, possible minimal time of 4 h at 10–20 rpm).
Centrifuge the 50 mL tube containing the bronchi at 500 × g for 5 min and 4°C.
Gently aspirate the supernatant, leaving 20 mL in the tube.
Pass the remaining 20 mL through an autoclaved stainless strainer with a minimum of 100 μm pore size to the 50 mL container/tube.
Add 20 mL of DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC medium to neutralize the remaining Pronase.
Shake to mix well, then vortex for 2 min.
Put the content of the tube into a 15 cm Petri dish.
Bisect the lung explant with a sterile scalpel.
Scrape cells from the inside (lumen side) of the explant using the scalpel blade.
Rinse the scalpel and bronchi with DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC to recover as many cells as possible.
Repeat rinsing twice.
Aspirate the medium containing cells, and transfer to a 50 mL container/tube through a stainless-steel strainer.
Rinse the Petri dish again with remaining DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC; recover the medium too.
Centrifuge the whole content of the recovered medium cell solution in a fresh 50 mL tube at 500 × g, 5 min, and 4°C.
Gently aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add trypsin to dislodge cells based on pellet size.
Resuspend the cells by gently pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 7 minutes at 37°C.
Add up to 5 mL of DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC and mix the cells by gentle pipetting.
Centrifuge 500 × g, 4°C, for 5 minutes.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add amplification media depending on the size of the pellet, between 2 and 5 mL, and resuspend well with the pipette.
Place 15 μL of the cell suspension on a counting chamber and count the cells.
Add 10 mL amplification medium to a collagen-coated 75 cm² flask.
Seed 500,000 cells per 75 cm² flask.
Put the flasks into the incubator at 37°C.
Aspirate transport medium from polyp samples carefully, avoiding small polyps.
Place the polyp in an empty 50 mL falcon tube.
Wash the polyp to eliminate blood cells by adding 25 mL of PBS-DTT and shaking manually for 1 minute.
Aspirate the medium after washing with PBS-DTT.
Repeat steps i. and ii. to ensure thorough removal of blood cells.
Rinse the polyp to remove DTT by adding 25 mL of PBS-FTVC and shaking for 1 minute.
Aspirate the medium after rinsing with PBS-FTVC.
Repeat steps i. and ii. to ensure thorough removal of DTT solution.
Take 14 mL from the 50 mL tube containing DMEM/F12-FTVC medium and add it to polyp.
Add 4 mL of Pronase to the 36 mL of DMEM/F12-FTVC in another 50 mL tube.
Transfer the polyp into the DMEM/F12-FTVC-Pronase solution.
Incubate the polyp overnight at 4°C on a rotator, at 10–20 rpm if adjustable.
Centrifuge the tube containing the polyp at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C the next day.
Gently aspirate the supernatant, leaving 20 mL in the tube.
Add 20 mL of DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC medium to neutralize the remaining Pronase.
Shake to mix well and vortex for 2 min at half-speed.
Pass the content (polyp and medium) into a 15 cm Petri dish through a stainless-steel strainer.
Rinse the polyp with 5 mL of DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC using fast flow from the pipette.
Repeat the rinsing step twice.
Aspirate the medium containing cells and transfer to the initial 50 mL Falcon tube through the strainer.
Rinse the Petri dish again with DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC; recover the medium as indicated in previous steps.
Centrifuge the whole content at 1,500 rpm, for 5 minutes, and at 4°C.
Gently aspirate the supernatant.
Add between 1 to 2 mL of trypsin (use 2 mL if required for larger pellet size).
Resuspend the cells and leave for 7 minutes at 37°C.
Add 5 mL of DMEM/F12-FBS20%-FTVC and gently resuspend by pipetting.
Centrifuge at 500 × g, for 5 minutes, and at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add amplification medium (depending on pellet size) to resuspend the cells using a pipette.
Place 15 μL of cell suspension on a counting chamber to count the cells.
Put 500,000 cells per 75 cm² flask, filled with 10 mL of amplification medium.
Place flasks into the incubator until next day.
Aspirate the medium from the 75 cm² or 25 cm² flask.
Rinse with 10 mL of PBS-FTVC.
Aspirate the PBS-FTVC.
Add fresh amplification medium (10 mL for a T75 flask, 5 mL for a T25 flask).
Inspect the cells every day for adherence and shape.
Monitor cell growth and quality of the medium.
Change the medium every 48–72 hours.
Aspirate medium.
Add fresh 10 mL amplification medium to a T75 flask or 5 mL to a T25 flask.
Monitor cells for expansion, which can take from 3 to 5 days depending on cell number.
Passage cells when they reach 80%–90% confluence.
If expansion takes longer than 10 days, the culture might not be successful.
If medium becomes cloudy, sample and send aliquots to microbiology department for bacterial analysis.
Rinse cells in the flask with 10 mL adapted PBS-FTVC if contamination is suspected.
Add 10 mL of amplification medium with antibiotics indicated in the antibiogram or Ciprofloxacin if no specific antibiotic information is available.
Notify lab manager about possible medium and incubator contamination.
Follow laboratory procedures for disinfection and isolation of exposed flasks.
Aspirate and discard culture medium from the 75 cm² culture flask.
Add 10 mL of PBS to the cell culture flask.
Aspirate and discard PBS.
Add 2 mL of Trypsin for a 75 cm² flask, and leave for 7 min at 37°C.
Tap the flask firmly with the palm of the hand to help the cells detach.
Keep the flask in a horizontal position during detachment.
Add 10 mL of amplification medium to stop the enzymatic reaction.
Vigorously rinse the flask using a 10 mL pipette to draw up and expel amplification medium over the flask surface.
Check the trypsinized flask under the microscope for remaining cells.
If many cells are still attached, repeat trypsinization by adding 2 mL of trypsin and incubating at 37°C for 5 minutes maximum.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant from the tube.
Add 3–5 mL of amplification medium depending on the size of the pellet in the tube.
Resuspend the pellet with a 10 mL pipette.
Take 15 μL of the cell suspension, place it on a cell-counting chamber, count cells, and calculate cell density.
Prepare a 24-well plate with the desired number of collagen-coated filters.
Maintain the filters before air-liquid (ALI) interface for 30 min to few hours, depending on the number of filter plates.
Exchange apical medium for fresh 300 μL amplification medium if left longer than day 2–3 until cells fill up the filter area.
Change basal medium every 48–72 h.
Aspirate and discard basal medium and add 900 μL of fresh ALI medium.
If the medium is cloudy and suspected of contamination, collect the medium and send it for testing in the bacteriology department.
Aspirate and discard apical medium if it appears cloudy before starting ALI culture.
Rinse with 300 μL adapted PBS-FTVC if apical medium is cloudy.
Add fresh 300 μL amplification medium with a change of antibiotics according to the antibiogram after rinsing.
Initiate ALI phase by aspirating and discarding apical medium and adding 900 μL of fresh ALI medium in basal part of well.
Change basal medium every 48–72 hours once ALI is initiated.
Remove CIPROFLOXACIN and AMINOGLYCOSIDE ANTIBIOTICS from the culture medium five days before planned.
Turn the Power on, on the EVOM2.
Sterilize the electrode with 70% ethanol and air dry.
Connect the electrode to the meter.
Set the Function switch to Ohms.
Turn the Mode Switch to R.
Turn the range switch to 20k (kΩ, ×1000 = Ω).
Measure the blank resistance and record the value (R blank).
Place the short electrode in the insert (apical compartment) and the longer arm of the electrode in the basolateral compartment.
Push the measure R button.
Record the resistance value in kΩ.
Measure R sample as indicated.
Repeat measurements for duplicates.
Perform measurements quickly to minimize temperature impact.
Place culture plate on a 37°C heat block during measurement.
Calculate the reading: (R sample Ω - R blank Ω) × 0.33 cm².
Clean and dry the electrode after use.
Store the cleaned electrode properly.
Add sterile physiological saline solution (∼100 μL) to the apical side for TEER measurements under ALI conditions.
Remove added saline solution after measurement to return to ALI condition.
Prepare freezing medium according to protocol specifications.
Prepare cryotubes with subject identification details as per local site policy.
Freeze cells at P0 or no higher than P2.
Aspirate and discard medium from the flask.
Add 10 mL of PBS to remove residual medium, then discard PBS.
Add 2 mL of trypsin to the flask and incubate for 7 minutes.
Tap the flask gently with your palm to help cells detach.
Transfer the suspension to a 50 mL tube after detaching cells completely.
Centrifuge at 500 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend cell pellet in regular medium as needed.
Count and spin down all cells in the tube.
Distribute around 1–2 × 10^6 cells per mL of freezing medium into cryovials.
Re-distribute equal amounts of cell suspension to each cryotube.
Place the cryovials in Mr. Frosty and put them into a −80°C freezer.
Move the preserved sample to the nitrogen storage container.
Defrost cryovials in a water bath at 37°C for up to 2 minutes.
Wipe the vial with alcohol and note the label information before proceeding.
Transfer defrosted cells to a 15 mL tube using a 1 mL pipette.
Add 1 mL of warm amplification medium drop-wise.
Wait one minute, then add another 1 mL of amplification medium and wait an additional minute.
Fill the tube with 10 mL of amplification medium and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 230 x g.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in amplification medium to achieve a cell density of at least 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Seed up to 2 million cells into a 75 cm² flask containing 10 mL amplification medium.
Seed up to 4 million cells into a 150 cm² flask containing 15 mL amplification medium.
Place the flasks in the 37°C incubator and observe cell expansion over the course of the next 2–3 days.
